rules.label: the method first publishes ANY escalation it has the vocabulary for: VERY_HIGH, or a RISING 24 h state change
rules.constant_provenance: A disjunction of two constants that both predate this change and are both untouched by it: susceptibility.BAND_EDGES's top edge (p90, USGS WaterWatch convention) and trend.FLOW_STEADY_FRACTION_PER_H (1 %/h, the STEADY band v1 and v2 share). Neither was chosen by looking at where Event Zero crossed it.
rules.note: This is the arm-level question — EARLIEST ESCALATION OF ANY KIND — and it is the only rule here under which a lead time is meaningful, because the two arms do not have the same vocabulary. Under @0.1.0 the second disjunct is unanswerable and the rule reduces to the band, which is not a handicap imposed by the harness: having no velocity statement at all is the defect under test. A reader must still see the per-rule breakdown, because the two disjuncts are different KINDS of statement — a level and a rate — and a single earliest-instant number hides which one fired.
